mstts:express-as.prosody: Hey there, and welcome. I’m glad you’re joining me for this journey—because what we’re about to explore together might just change the way you see America’s story. You know, we often hear that America is the land of opportunity, a place where anyone can rise above their circumstances. But have you ever wondered if that’s really the whole truth? Class divisions have been woven into the very fabric of American life, shaping who gets ahead and who’s left behind. And yet, we don’t talk about it all that much, do we? That’s where Nancy Isenberg’s White Trash: The 400-Year Untold History of Class in America comes in. She peels back the layers of history, showing how the dream of a classless society has always been more myth than reality. Together, we’ll trace the journey of America’s so-called “waste people”—from the days of the first British colonies, through Civil War battlefields, to the rise of trailer parks in the modern era. Along the way, we’ll uncover how privilege, exclusion, and aspiration have played out across generations, and how the label “white trash” became such a powerful symbol of marginalization. Isenberg’s work challenges us to rethink everything we think we know about equal opportunity and social mobility. We’ll see how language, politics, and cultural attitudes have shaped—and sometimes trapped—poor whites, keeping class boundaries firmly in place. So, if you’re ready to question old myths and dive into the hidden histories shaping identity, power, and opportunity in the United States, you’re in the right place. Let’s get started, and see what we can discover together.
